newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch May producer prices rise 2.7 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Dutch May producer prices rise 2.7 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The Dutch producer price index (PPI) for manufactured goods rose a provisional 0.8 percent in May from April, giving a 2.7 percent rise year-on-year, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said.
DUTCH PRODUCER PRICES May 97 April 97 May 96
The CBS said the higher price level was caused mainly by more expensive pork and by the increase in the prices of oil products.
Pork prices were 15 percent above those of May 1996, the CBS said. It added the price of veal, mainly for export, had also risen.
This contributed to the five percent rise year-on-year of food product prices in May. On a monthly basis, they rose 1.6 percent.
In the oil processing industry, prices rose 2.4 percent in May compared with April, while the increase amounted to 7.0 percent on an annual basis.
The 1.5 percent monthly rise in the overall price levels of industrial commodities and semi-manufactured products in May was caused by the higher prices of agricultural products, the CBS said.
These prices have risen 4.4 percent since May last year.
